name: Internal Tibial Torsion
definition: Internal rotation of the tibia causing intoeing gait, common in toddlers and usually improving spontaneously with growth.

investigations.principle: Imaging is rarely needed in typical developmental cases.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, physeal, occult injury, deformity or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Corrective osteotomy is reserved for severe persistent deformity in older children.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Jangha rotational phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Internal rotation of the tibia causing intoeing gait, common in toddlers and usually improving spontaneously with growth.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, open injury, severe deformity, rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, suspected infection or other listed red flags.
